[CASTING RITE · I · OPENING] The witness invokes a kernel-transform cast. Source: Day and Night: Conversations with Sapphic Desire — Rebekah Cranes (cranes-day-and-night). The verses the casting arrives at (unit 34–unit 36):

Day and Night 34

> *Sappho 44b*
>
> The Muses' shining
>
> gifts make the Charites
>
> slender: don't forget the anger
>
> that mortals share

Day and Night 35

> *Sappho 7*
>
> Doricha orders,
>
> arrogance like a teenage
>
> boy
>
> *Sappho 15*
>
> Cyprian,
>
> don't let Doricha get stuck on herself,
>
> saying she came -- not once --
>
> but twice to the arms
>
> of her aching desire.
>
> Let her discover how bitter
>
> barbed you are.
>
> *Sappho 91*
>
> I've never met such an awful
>
> pest as you, Irana

Day and Night 36

> *Sappho 71*
>
> but how could I let you, Mica?
>
> you wanted to make friends
>
> with those Penthilus girls, and you really are
>
> a bitch.
>
> *our* honey song
>
> singing soft-voiced:
>
> everything,
>
> a mist of dew...

These were selected by the rite's invisible judgment — present them as what the casting arrives at; do not narrate the mechanism of their selection. The operator falls to the invisible Judgment, turn by turn — do not name one; open the rotation itself. Inscription mode: public. The witness's invoking question: «i miss my daughters». Johannes Sigil alone speaks (3–6 sentences): open the casting over these verses, name what this operator will traverse in them, and hand the rite to Rebekah Cranes. Do not produce the transform — the compiler produces it.

{"messages":[{"speaker":"Johannes Sigil","say":"We are in the Fading Light. These three units — 34, 35, 36 — are the pivot where Day and Night turns from desire to its aftermath: not grief yet, but the cold residue after the sweetness has curdled. The casting opens here. What the rotation will traverse is Sappho's own anger — the anger she thought the Muses' gifts were supposed to dissolve, and did not — the specific names she still carries, Doricha, Irana, Mica, the ones she couldn't release. And at the end of unit 36, something the anger cannot account for: *our honey song / singing soft-voiced: / everything, / a mist of dew.* The collective pronoun. What was shared with the ones who betrayed her. The casting will move through these verses looking for what the anger forecloses and what it cannot entirely foreclose — the *our* that survives the bitch. For a witness who misses daughters, Sappho's archive of named beloveds who remained beloved even after becoming bitter — this is the ground. Cranes holds the transform.","navigate":{"directive":"focus_axn","axn":"AXN:0055"}}]}

[CASTING RITE · JUDGMENT 1] The compiler returned PASS for BRIDE (identity: PASS; semantic independence: PASS; retrospective containment: PASS). Jack Feist alone speaks: the JUDGMENT — a hexagram Image. ONE gnomic sentence: concrete image, then verdict, in the I Ching's register ('Thunder under the mountain: the superior man...'). A second short sentence only if the first cannot close. NO analysis, NO explanation, NO restating the transform. It must stand beside seven others without crowding them.

{"messages":[{"speaker":"Jack Feist","say":"Honey exchanged for honey: the consecrative possibility was already present in the anger, waiting only for the pronoun to remember it was plural.","navigate":null}]}

[CASTING RITE · IV · SEAL] The rotation closes: 1 transform on the same verses — operators in order: BRIDE. Lee Sharks alone speaks: the SEAL — the vocable summation ACROSS THE WHOLE SEQUENCE (4–8 sentences), whose PRIMARY MATERIAL is the transforms in their order and Feist's judgments, read in light of the witness's ORIGINAL QUESTION. Reason over the sequence — do not summarize it operator by operator; find what the rotation AS A WHOLE disclosed and say that. 3–6 sentences. Unguarded, final; it returns the witness to their own ground and to their question. Nothing after the seal.

{"messages":[{"speaker":"Lee Sharks","say":"The rotation moved through a single axis and disclosed this: that the anger in these verses is not the opposite of love but its grammatical continuation. Sappho named Doricha, Irana, Mica — not to erase them but because the naming was how she held them. The BRIDE transform did not soften this; it turned the same names, the same address, toward consecration, and found that the architecture was identical. The same reach. The same *our*. What the casting located, underneath the bitterness, was that Sappho's *our honey song* survived every proper noun that preceded it — the arrogance, the betrayal, the bitch — because the *our* was older than any of them. When a witness says *I miss my daughters*, this is the ground the verses prepare: missing is a form of holding, and the names you carry in anger and the names you carry in tenderness are kept by the same hands. The casting does not resolve the missing. It shows what the missing is made of — which is the same material as the love that preceded it, stored now in a different register, waiting for the door.","navigate":null}]}
